statement: Let (X, B) be a smooth compact Kähler klt pair with rational simple normal crossing boundary. Suppose KX + B ∼Q P + R, P semiample, R = N(KX + B) ≥ 0 with P, R rational. A finite ordinary (KX + B)-negative program reaches a normal compact Kähler klt model on which the log canonical line is semiample. Its steps contract or flip detected analytic extremal rays, are P-trivial, and preserve a fixed generated Cartier multiple of P as an actual line. The final adjoint is rationally linearly equivalent to the descended semiample line. The steps extract no divisors; on a common resolution the initial adjoint equals the pullback of the final adjoint plus an effective divisor exceptional over the final model.
